o Motor drives are the core technology for EVs that convert the on-board
electrical energy to the desired mechanical motion. Meanwhile, electric
machines are the key element of motor drive technology. The requirements of
electric machines for EVs are much more demanding than that for industrial
applications.

slides.title: Electrical machines – Automotive demanding requirements
Electric Drive
slides.body:
An electric drive can be defined as an electromechanical device for converting electrical energy into
mechanical energy to impart motion to different machines and mechanisms for various kinds of process
control.

slides.title: Components of an electric drive
slides.body:
The basic architecture of a motion control system
includes:
1. Power source : provides the energy to the
drive system
2. Power converter : interfaces the motor with
the power source and provides the motor with
adjustable voltage, current and/or frequency.
3. Controller: by comparing the input command
for speed and/or position with the actual values
measured through sensors, provides appropriate
control signals to the power converter.

slides.title: Components of an electric drive
slides.body:
4. Electric motor : selected according to the power
level, environmental factors and performance required
by the load.
5. One or more feedback sensors to return the
position and/or velocity of the actuator to the motion
controller in order to close the position and/or velocity
control loops.
6. Mechanical components to transform the motion
of the actuator into the desired load motion, including:
gears, shafting, ball screw, belts, linkages, and linear
and rotational bearings.

slides.title: Electromotive force
slides.body:
In a motor, the induced emf always acts to reduce the current in the loop. That’s why it is called
“back emf.”
In fact, Faraday-Neumann-Lenz law establish that the induced current in a loop is in the direction
that creates a magnetic field that opposes the change in magnetic flux through the area
enclosed by the loop. The induced current tends to keep the original magnetic flux through the
circuit from changing.

slides.title: Electric Motors
slides.body:
An electric motor converts electrical energy to mechanical
energy. It consists in a cylindrical structure with a fixed,
static part, called stator, and a moving, rotating one, the
rotor.
Both the structures can be populated with either windings
or permanent magnets, achieveing different electrical and
magnetic performances.
The energy conversion happens in the interaction
between the magnetic fields of the two structures, which
produces a net output torque.

slides.title: DC Machine
slides.body:
The stator, external, equipped with salient poles, works as an inductor and
can be realized:
- with excitation windings arranged around the pole bodies; such
windings are crossed by direct current and are connected to each other in
controversial series to generate magnetic polarity of alternating sign from
one pole to the next;
- with permanent magnets.
The internal rotor, consisting of a cylinder of magnetic material, works as
armature; on the periphery of the rotor are uniformly distributed slots where
the active conductors are housed. The set of active conductors (connected in
series with each other) constitutes a closed circuit.

slides.title: DC Machine
slides.body:
The part in the air between stator and rotor is called air gap, in this area the
field magnetic has the greatest intensity.
The commutator is mounted on the same shaft as the rotor. This is for the
purpose of supply the windings with the power supply voltage and ensure
that the torque generated by the current that passes through is constant or at
least unidirectional.
The brushes crawl on the collector and electrically connect it to the external
terminals of the machine.
The presence of the system commutator-brushes causes various issues,
mainly the continuous maintenance required and the undesired sparking.

If current always flows in the same direction, then the loop will only oscillate rather than rotate. Here
come in play the commutator-brushes system, which reverse the direction of the current on each half
cycle in order to make the rotor rotate.
Now the torque is always applied in the same direction inducing the loop to spin continuously.

slides.title: DC Machine – Equivalent circuit
slides.body:
The excitation circuit is implied, it is hidden in the
electromotive force at the ends of the brushes (index of
the rotation of the rotor inside the stator poles).
The electromotive force E represents an active load.
Ra is the resistance of the armature winding ( La, armature
inductance, in steady state does not come into play) and
the resistance associated with the collector brush contact.
Va is the armature voltage, Ia the armature current, Ke the
machine constant, ω the angular velocity, ϕ the excitation
flux per pole.

slides.title: Speed regulation
slides.body:
There are three ways to adjust the speed:
- Act on the armature voltage (separated excitation only)
- Act on the flow of excitation
- Act on the armature resistance
These actions can be carried out individually or jointly, each being effective in a different speed range.
The armature current is controlled when you want to have the maximum output torque of the machine.

slides.title: Speed regulation – Armature voltage
slides.body:
By varying the voltage the constant term varies, which means that the speed when the torque is zero
depends on V. If V reduces the point of intersection of the characteristic with the axis ω is reduced, it
moves, but the characteristic remains parallel (the characteristics translate parallel to the nominal one).
If we increase the V, the ω increases.

slides.title: DC Machine - Breaking
slides.body:
If the directions of the voltages and currents are those shown in the figure, the machine acts as a motor
(switch closed). If the E is made greater than V, the armature current is reversed, the excitation flux has
remained with its polarity and the machine switches to operate as a brake because the torque reverses
becoming negative and instead of being a driving force it becomes braking. Therefore, the machine acts as a
brake towards the load and from the electrical point of view it acts as a generator, takes energy from the load,
converts it into electricity and this can be dissipated or recovered.

slides.title: DC Machine
slides.body:
Pros:
- Simple operation and motor control
- Cheapest and simplest motor
- Speed proportional to voltage
Cons:
- Requires high maintenance
- Sparking
- Low-life span (due to physical wear on brushes)
DC motor drive technology is very mature and well developed. However, with the ever-increasing
demand on high efficiency, high power density, and maintenance-free operation, DC motor drives are
no longer attractive for EV propulsion.
